slot.brief: Two related quantities changing with time (e.g., ladder sliding, water level rising); differentiate an implicit relation and evaluate at a given instant.

stem: An upright right circular frustum-shaped tank is $6$ m high, with bottom and top radii $2$ m and $5$ m. Water enters at $6\pi\ \text{m}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$. When the water is $2$ m deep, find the rate of increase of the wetted curved area.

verdicts.working: At depth h, the water-surface radius is r=2+h/2. Since dV/dh=πr², at h=2 we have dh/dt=6π/(9π)=2/3. The wetted curved area is A=π(2+r)(h√5/2), so at h=2, dA/dh=3π√5. Thus dA/dt=2π√5 m² min⁻¹.

working:
Let $h$ be water depth and $r=2+\dfrac h2$ the water-surface radius. The wetted slant height is $s=\dfrac{\sqrt5}{2}h$. $\dfrac{dV}{dh}=\pi r^2$, hence at $h=2$, $r=3$ and $\dfrac{dh}{dt}=\dfrac{6\pi}{9\pi}=\dfrac23$. $S=\pi(2+r)s=\pi\sqrt5(2h+\dfrac{h^2}{4})$. Thus $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=\pi\sqrt5(2+\dfrac h2)\dfrac{dh}{dt}=2\pi\sqrt5\ \text{m}^2\text{ min}^{-1}$.

Independent check: At depth h, the water-surface radius is r=2+h/2. Since dV/dh=πr², at h=2 we have dh/dt=6π/(9π)=2/3. The wetted curved area is A=π(2+r)(h√5/2), so at h=2, dA/dh=3π√5. Thus dA/dt=2π√5 m² min⁻¹.
solution:
At depth $h$, the water-surface radius is $r=2+\dfrac h2$, and $\dfrac{dV}{dh}=\pi r^2$. At $h=2$, $r=3$, so $\dfrac{dh}{dt}=\dfrac{6\pi}{9\pi}=\dfrac23$.
The wetted curved area is $S=\pi(2+r)\dfrac{\sqrt5}{2}h=\pi\sqrt5\left(2h+\dfrac{h^2}{4}\right)$. Hence
$$\dfrac{dS}{dt}=\pi\sqrt5\left(2+\dfrac h2\right)\dfrac{dh}{dt}=2\pi\sqrt5\ \text{m}^2\text{ min}^{-1}.$$
